h1: The 8 Best Rice Cookers Under $200 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Rice Cooker Under $200 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best rice cookers under $200, from Zojirushi Micom models to AROMA multicookers that cost a fraction as much.
summary: The Zojirushi NS-TSC18 is the pick for families, with Micom fuzzy-logic controls and a 1.8 liter pot. The NS-TPC10XT suits buyers who want a PFAS-free nonstick pot, the 3-cup Micom is the compact choice, and the AROMA multicookers are the value play for anyone who wants steam and slow-cook modes for far less.
intro: A $200 ceiling is generous for a rice cooker, and the most expensive buying mistake is assuming the highest price bucket is automatically right for you. A household of one rarely needs a 1.8 liter machine.

We ranked eight cookers from their listings: capacity, control type, pot material and extra modes. Micom fuzzy-logic controls are the big divider, so the list starts there and works down to simple, cheap models.

products.name: Zojirushi NS-TSC18 Micom Rice Cooker and Warmer, 1.8 Liters
products.verdict: The largest Micom fuzzy-logic cooker in the lineup, built for families.
products.description:
The NS-TSC18 is a rice cooker and warmer with Micom fuzzy-logic controls and a 1.8 liter capacity, priced in the $100-200 bracket.

It takes first place because it carries Micom control at the largest size here. The 5.5-cup NS-TPC10XT below has the same control type in a smaller pot, so this one is the better fit for larger households.

Buy it if you cook rice most nights for several people. Caveat: it is the biggest machine of the group and takes counter space.
products.idealFor: Families that cook rice nearly every day.
products.skipIf: You cook for one or two.

products.name: Zojirushi NS-TPC10XT Micom Rice Cooker & Warmer (with PFAS-Free Nonstick), 5.5-Cup, Stainless Brown
products.verdict: Micom control with a PFAS-free nonstick inner pot.
products.description:
This 5.5-cup cooker and warmer uses Micom fuzzy-logic controls and a PFAS-free nonstick inner pot, in a stainless brown finish. It sits in the $100-200 bracket.

It ranks second because the coating is the only reason to choose it over the NS-TSC18, which has more capacity. Mid-size households get the most from it.

Best for anyone who wants to avoid PFAS in their cookware. Caveat: the pot is smaller than the NS-TSC18's.

products.name: Zojirushi Micom 3-Cup Compact Size Rice Cooker and Warmer, Stainless Steel
products.verdict: Micom control in a 3-cup body with a retractable cord.
products.description:
This is a 3-cup Micom rice cooker and warmer with a stainless steel body, multiple settings and a built-in retractable power cord. It is easy to transport and sits in the $100-200 bracket.

It ranks below the larger Micom models because capacity is limited to 3 cups. It beats the basic 3-cup Zojirushi because it adds fuzzy-logic control.

Great for singles, couples and small kitchens. Caveat: small batches only.
products.idealFor: Singles and couples in small kitchens.

products.name: Zojirushi 6-Cup Rice Cooker
products.verdict: A 6-cup Zojirushi for buyers who skip Micom sensing.
products.description:
The 6-cup Zojirushi is a straightforward cooker priced in the $50-100 bracket, with no Micom controls listed.

It ranks fourth because it undercuts the Micom models on price while keeping the brand. It beats the AROMA units on brand reliability, but trails them on modes.

A fit for a larger household that wants a simpler machine. Caveat: the listing names no advanced cooking modes.
products.idealFor: Larger households that prefer simple controls.

products.name: Zojirushi 3 Cup Rice Cooker/Steamer (White)
products.verdict: Zojirushi's compact basic cooker with a steamer function.
products.description:
This 3-cup rice cooker and steamer combo comes in white and falls in the $50-100 bracket. No Micom control is listed.

It ranks fifth because it is the same idea as the 6-cup model at half the size. It costs less than the 3-cup Micom, which is its argument.

Good for one or two people who want a steamer in a compact machine. Caveat: it has no advanced controls.
products.idealFor: One or two people wanting a simple steamer.

products.award: Best for Big Households on a Budget
products.name: AROMA Digital Rice Cooker, 4-Cup (Uncooked) / 8-Cup (Cooked), ARC-914SBD
products.verdict: Digital controls, steamer and grain modes at a budget price.
products.description:
The ARC-914SBD is a 2 quart digital cooker with 4-cup uncooked and 8-cup cooked capacity, a stainless exterior, and steamer, grain cooker and multicooker functions. It is in the $25-50 bracket.

It ranks sixth because it trades Micom sensing for a low price and wide function range. It offers more modes than any Zojirushi on this list except the pricier ones.

Pick it for a bigger household on a small budget. Caveat: it uses digital, not fuzzy-logic, control.

products.name: AROMA Digital Rice Cooker, 4-Cup (Uncooked) / 8-Cup (Cooked), 2 Qt, Multicooker
products.verdict: Adds slow-cook and oatmeal modes for a very low cost.
products.description:
This 2 quart digital cooker has 4-cup uncooked and 8-cup cooked capacity, with steam and multicook modes plus slow-cook and oatmeal-cook modes, auto keep-warm and a stainless exterior. It is in the $25-50 bracket.

It ranks just below the ARC-914SBD in this list but is the more flexible pick, with slow-cook and oatmeal added. That is the tradeoff against Micom machines that focus on rice.

Best for cooks who want one appliance for more than rice. Caveat: rice quality is not the focus.
products.idealFor: Cooks wanting one appliance for many uses.
products.skipIf: Perfect rice is your only goal.

products.name: AROMA Rice Cooker, 3-Cup (Uncooked) / 6-Cup (Cooked), ARC-363NG
products.verdict: A 1.5 quart cooker that also makes oatmeal and soup, for under $25.
products.description:
The ARC-363NG has 3-cup uncooked and 6-cup cooked capacity in a 1.5 quart bowl, with auto keep-warm. It doubles as an oatmeal cooker and soup maker, and costs under $25.

It ranks last because it is the simplest pick. It is the cheapest option in the list by a clear margin.

Fits students and singles on a minimal budget. Caveat: it is small and basic.
products.idealFor: Students and singles on a minimal budget.
products.skipIf: You cook for more than two.

whatMatters.detail: Micom means a microcomputer adjusts cooking time and heat. It helps with different rice types and small batches. Look for the word Micom in the title.
Cup ratings refer to uncooked rice, and cooked yield is roughly double. Buying too big wastes counter space. Match the number to the household you actually feed.
Some pots are PFAS-free nonstick. This matters if you prefer to avoid those coatings. Check the title or specs for the coating claim.
Slow-cook, steam and oatmeal modes turn a rice cooker into a general appliance. They matter if kitchen space is limited. Read the title for the mode list.
A warmer holds rice ready after cooking. It matters if meals are staggered. Look for warmer or keep-warm in the listing.

faq.q: Does every Zojirushi here have Micom?
faq.a: No. The 6-cup and 3-cup white models list no Micom controls. The NS-TSC18, NS-TPC10XT and the 3-cup Micom do.
Buying by price bucket instead of household size. A 1.8 liter machine is wasted on one person.

faq.q: Is Micom worth it over an AROMA?
faq.a: If rice is a staple, yes. If you want multiple modes cheaply, an AROMA is better value.

faq.q: How do I measure the rice?
faq.a: Use the cup that comes with the cooker, since cup sizes differ from standard US cups.

faq.q: How do I clean the pot?
faq.a: Wash it by hand with a soft sponge, especially nonstick pots, and dry before use.

faq.q: Can I cook oatmeal in these?
faq.a: The AROMA models list oatmeal modes. Zojirushi listings here do not.

finalTake: Buy the Zojirushi NS-TSC18 if you cook rice often and for several people. Choose the NS-TPC10XT if the pot coating matters. For a limited budget, the AROMA ARC-914SBD is the one to beat.
